why: the C-Spin section quotes harddrop in prose; a wiki sentence with no committed copy is a figure whose only home is prose, and nothing re-derives it.
provenance_standard: Both revisions carry MediaWiki's OWN rev_sha1 AND a sha1 recomputed here from action=raw. Two independent authorities that agree — the cvc5 standard, not z3's trust-on-first-use. Reproduce: sha1 of the action=raw body, CRLF->LF, trailing newline stripped.
the_count_trap: `replaces_the_double` is set by READING each continuation, never by counting headings. Counting them gave 'six non-Double continuations', which is false and shipped to seven reports before this file was written: LST Stacking and T-Spin Triple Tower both describe what happens AFTER a T-Spin Double, and Trinity / STSD branches on whether the TSD was already done, so all three still produce the Double the ordering metric counts. Of the 7 continuations, exactly 1 replaces it.

pages.lead: The C-Spin (TKI積み) is a kind of Triple Double Attack. It is invented by TKI. This name is given because of the "C" shape that is formed by the J and L. As the name suggests, it results in a T-Spin Triple which is usually followed by a T-Spin Double within three bags. As an opener, it is most often built with an ZST core whereas L and J are used to build the overhang.

continuations.heading: T-Spin Triple and Imperial Cross
continuations.first_sentence: No matter how wide the gap between the overhang and the stack on the right is, you can replace the T-Spin Double with a T-Spin Triple or Imperial Cross after the T-Spin Triple from any C-Spin setup.

continuations.heading: STMB Cave
continuations.first_sentence: The STMB Cave continuation will only work if the following cells in diagram 1 (marked with X's) are free.

continuations.heading: Trinity / STSD
continuations.first_sentence: If you used a J piece as the overhang and there is an S piece or nothing on the overhang, you can make a Trinity (if the TSD is not done beforehand) or STSD (if the TSD is done beforehand) by placing an S piece on the overhang.

continuations.heading: Fractal
continuations.first_sentence: If you have a 4-columns wide gap, you can place the third bag's Z and S pieces as the base, if the second Z piece was placed on the overhang.

continuations.heading: LST Stacking
continuations.first_sentence: Generally, if you have a 2-columns wide gap, you can follow with LST Stacking by placing an L piece on the overhang.

continuations.heading: T-Spin Triple Tower
continuations.first_sentence: If there is a Z piece on a J piece overhang, regardless if that Z piece is from the second or third bag, you can stack a T-Spin Triple Tower after a T-Spin Double.

pages.lead: The Triple Double attack, also known as Triple-Double, C-Spin, or abbreviated as TD, is a combo T-Spin setup that consists of a T-Spin Triple followed by a T-Spin Double.
pages.empty_field: Empty field Triple Double setups are also known as C-Spins.

the_tension: the two pages do not agree. Triple_Double_Attack_Setups equates an empty-field Triple Double with a C-Spin outright, which would make the ordering metric the wiki's own definition; C-Spin attributes the name to the C shape formed by J and L, says the Double is 'usually' the follow-up, and gives one continuation that replaces it. So Triple-then-Double OVER-counts and UNDER-counts. Recorded, not resolved: a wiki contradicting itself is not a licence to adopt the reading that flatters the metric.
